title: Adding one simplex gives a covering of semi-representable Hom objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a hypercover of $X$ in the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Let $U\subseteq V$ be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with $U_n$, $V_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n\geq0$ and with $U$ and $V$ having finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Suppose there are $n\geq0$ and $x\in V_n$, $x\notin U_n$, such that (1) $V_i=U_i$ for $i<n$, (2) $V_n=U_n\cup\{x\}$, and (3) every $z\in V_j$ with $j>n$ and $z\notin U_j$ is degenerate. Then the restriction morphism $\operatorname{Hom}(V,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] is a covering in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object].

source.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), statement and proof (via simplicial.tex Lemmas 018R, 017N, 018V)

proof.text: *Gluing the new simplex.* Let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set of order-preserving maps $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$, $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ the simplicial subset of the non-surjective ones, and $a:\Delta[n]\to V$, $a(\varphi)=V(\varphi)(x)$. Conditions (1)-(3) of the statement are those of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex], so $a$ maps $\partial\Delta[n]$ into $U$, and with $b:\partial\Delta[n]\to U$ the restriction of $a$ the square ($b$, $a$, $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$, $U\subseteq V$) is a pushout of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n=0$, $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty (every map $[m]\to[0]$ is surjective) and $V$ with the inclusion of $U$ and $a$ is a coproduct $U\amalg\Delta[0]$.

source.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), proof, first sentence ('V = U amalg Delta[0]') and second paragraph ('By Simplicial, Lemma 018R we have V = U amalg_{boundary Delta[n]} Delta[n]')

proof.text: *Notation and the Hom objects involved.* Call a simplicial set admissible if all its sets of $m$-simplices are finite and nonempty and it has finitely many nondegenerate simplices; $U$ and $V$ are admissible by hypothesis, $\Delta[n]$ is admissible for every $n\geq0$ and $\partial\Delta[n]$ for $n\geq1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex](a),(b). Write $H(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] and, for a morphism $f:S\to S'$ of admissible simplicial sets, $f^*:H(S')\to H(S)$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout]; the morphism to be shown a covering is $\rho=\iota^*:H(V)\to H(U)$, $\iota:U\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex](a) there is a unique isomorphism $\varepsilon:K_n\to H(\Delta[n])$ with $u^{\Delta[n]}_\varphi\circ\varepsilon=K(\varphi)$ for all $\varphi$ (both are $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta[n],K)_0$, unique up to unique isomorphism).

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph (the objects Hom(Delta[n],K)_0, Hom(boundary Delta[n],K)_0)

proof.text: *Isomorphisms are coverings.* If $(\alpha,(f_i)):\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ with inverse $(\beta,(g_j))$, then $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_I$, $\alpha\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}_J$, $g_{\alpha(i)}\circ f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{\beta(j)}\circ g_j=\mathrm{id}$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object], so $\alpha$ is bijective and each $f_i$ is an isomorphism; hence for each $j$ the family $\{f_i:\alpha(i)=j\}$ consists of the single isomorphism $f_{\beta(j)}$, which is etale and surjective, a covering family of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. So every isomorphism of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is a covering, and by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence](1) a composite $\sigma\circ c\circ\tau$ of a covering $c$ with isomorphisms $\sigma,\tau$ is a covering.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('this arrow is identified with K_n -> (cosk_{n-1} sk_{n-1} K)_n and hence is a covering'): the identification is by isomorphisms, which preserve coverings

proof.text: *Case $n\geq1$: the fibre square.* By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout](a), applied to $A=\partial\Delta[n]$, $B=U$, $C=\Delta[n]$, $D=V$ with $p=b$, $q$ the inclusion $j:\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ (all four admissible by step 2), $H(V)$ with $\rho$ and $a^*$ is a fibre product of $b^*:H(U)\to H(\partial\Delta[n])$ and $j^*:H(\Delta[n])\to H(\partial\Delta[n])$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('By Simplicial, Lemma 017N we get that ... is a fibre product square')

proof.text: *Case $n\geq1$: the bottom arrow is a covering.* Let $\theta:H(\partial\Delta[n])\to M_n(K)$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex](b) and $\rho_n:K_n\to H(\partial\Delta[n])$ the morphism of (c) there, so $\theta\circ\rho_n=\mu_n$. The morphism $j^*\circ\varepsilon$ satisfies $u^{\partial\Delta[n]}_\varphi\circ j^*\circ\varepsilon=u^{\Delta[n]}_\varphi\circ\varepsilon=K(\varphi)$ for every simplex $\varphi$ of $\partial\Delta[n]$, hence equals $\rho_n$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $H(\partial\Delta[n])$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object]. Thus $j^*=\theta^{-1}\circ\mu_n\circ\varepsilon^{-1}$. Since $K$ is a hypercover, $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$ is a covering [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object](5), so $j^*$ is a covering by step 3.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, last two sentences ('By Simplicial, Lemma 018V this arrow is identified with K_n -> (cosk_{n-1} sk_{n-1} K)_n and hence is a covering by definition of a hypercovering')

proof.text: *Case $n\geq1$: base change.* Let $P=H(U)\times_{H(\partial\Delta[n])}H(\Delta[n])$ be the fibre product of $b^*$ and $j^*$ constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits](2), with first projection $\mathrm{pr}_1:P\to H(U)$. By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence](2) (the covering $j^*$, base changed along $b^*$), $\mathrm{pr}_1$ is a covering. By step 4, $H(V)$ is also a fibre product of $b^*$ and $j^*$, so the unique morphism $\tau:H(V)\to P$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\tau=\rho$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\tau=a^*$ is an isomorphism. Hence $\rho=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\tau$ is a covering by step 3.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, second paragraph ('Thus it suffices to show that the bottom horizontal arrow is a covering'), with hypercovering.tex Lemma 01G4 (lemma-covering-permanence) (2) for the base change

proof.text: *Case $n=0$.* By step 1, $V=U\amalg\Delta[0]$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout](b) (with $A$ empty, $B=U$, $C=\Delta[0]$, $D=V$, admissible by step 2) $H(V)$ with $\rho$ and $a^*$ is a product of $H(U)$ and $H(\Delta[0])$. A product in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is a fibre product over the final object $e=\{\mathrm{id}_X\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits](1),(2), and $M_0(K)=e$ with $\mu_0:K_0\to e$ a covering since $K$ is a hypercover [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object](5). The unique morphism $H(\Delta[0])\to e$ is $\mu_0\circ\varepsilon^{-1}$, a covering by step 3. Let $P=H(U)\times_eH(\Delta[0])$ be the fibre product of [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits](2); its projection $\mathrm{pr}_1:P\to H(U)$ is a covering by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence](2), and as in step 6 $\rho=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\tau$ for the isomorphism $\tau:H(V)\to P$ comparing the two products, so $\rho$ is a covering by step 3.

source.place: Lemma 01GM, proof, first paragraph ('If n = 0 ... V = U amalg Delta[0]. In this case Hom(V,K)_0 = Hom(U,K)_0 x K_0. The result, in this case, then follows from Lemma 01G4')

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks 01GM. The source's three citations became nodes: 018R (glue one simplex: V = U amalg_{boundary} Delta[n]) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex; 017N (Hom(-,K)_0 turns the pushout into a fibre product, plus the product case over an empty A needed for n = 0) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-pushout; 018V with 0177 (Hom(Delta[n],K)_0 = K_n, Hom(boundary,K)_0 = M_n(K), restriction = mu_n) -> lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-standard-simplex, stated against the explicit matching object M_n(K) of def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object instead of cosk_{n-1}sk_{n-1}. Written out what the source leaves implicit: that isomorphisms of SR(X) are coverings (so the identifications preserve coverings), the base change through the canonical fibre product of lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits and covering permanence (1),(2), and the n = 0 case through the final object. Statement unchanged (it assumes V also has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, which the source does not need but which follows from (1)-(3)). No Lean on slopmaster2.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the fourth paragraph of lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement's proof ('Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries; the matching covers of U lift those boundaries after finite refinement') for one new simplex: step 1 and 4 the prescribed boundary (gluing along boundary Delta[n]), steps 5-6 the lift along the matching cover K_n -> M_n(K) by base change, step 7 the degree-0 case.
